0x30e299f132eaa2c5_0x1a8f1c74d5ee1fb3.text: Okay, finally a review! It's been a week since I said goodbye to glasses! ...Many people might wonder why I decided to get LASIK. To be honest, I was tired of wearing glasses. I personally had three pairs of glasses that I'd leave lying around the room, sometimes I couldn't find them, sometimes I'd forget them. So, I decided to get it done two days before the procedure – I booked an appointment right away. For this LASIK procedure, I had it done with Dr. Namphueng at Thonburi Bamrungmuang Hospital. I chose the femto LASIK technique, which uses a laser for surgery. ...Before the procedure, the nurse initially measured my corneal thickness, intraocular pressure, etc., to prepare for meeting the doctor. Initially, my cornea was slightly thinner than average, and I almost didn't get the femto technique. But the nurse said, "Wait until you see the doctor, and they'll reassess." ...Once I met the doctor, she assessed my cornea and said it was fine, which was a huge relief. I chose this technique because it has a shorter recovery time. For my profession, I didn't want a long recovery period because a long recovery means losing income. However, for those whose cornea is very thin after the procedure, the doctor will recommend the regular LASIK technique. (Which means a longer recovery period.) Before the surgery, the doctor will give you a consultation and do a detailed eye exam to determine how clear you want your eyes to be and how comfortable you want them to be. The doctor measures very precisely, even down to adjusting the angle of your eyes. It's amazing! …During the surgery, I wasn't very worried, the only thing I felt was cold. Maybe it's because I'm someone who gets cold easily, and the air conditioning in the operating room was so cold that I had to ask the nurse for a blanket. During the surgery, there wasn't much to it. The doctor would have me look at a single point of light. The nurse would put anesthetic eye drops in before the surgery, so there's no need to worry about pain or anything. It didn't hurt at all during the procedure. But when you see something close to your eye, it feels a little strange. But the nurses were great, they built up the atmosphere so well, it was amazing. The doctor was also great, constantly telling me, "I'm going to fire the laser now," "I'm firing it now," "Counting down 9 seconds." They explained every step, which really eased my anxiety. But, I have to whisper, when they fired the laser, it smelled like burning fuse, like using a mosquito swatter. Hahaha. That's it. 10 or 15 seconds. I think the whole procedure for both eyes took less than 15 minutes, or maybe even faster. I'm not sure, but it felt like it didn't take long at all. It was amazing! …The post-procedure symptoms were eye irritation, like dry eyes all the time. The doctor advised me to sleep and avoid using my eyes for 4-6 hours. After sleeping, when I woke up, wow, my vision was starting to clear up to about 80% (as far as I could see through the eye shields). I woke up, ate, took my medicine, and went back to sleep. The first day I woke up, I took off the eye shields, and I could see like crazy! Crystal clear, full HD! A thought flashed through my mind: "I should have done this a long time ago!!!!" I don't know what I was afraid of. …Today marks one week since the procedure, and I feel like my vision is almost 100%, but at night, when I look at lights, they still appear blurry. The doctor said this is normal and will gradually improve after a week. …From the moment I had the procedure until now, I feel I made the right decision to get LASIK with Dr. Namphueng. The doctor is kind and explained everything clearly. The nurses and staff are all lovely, especially the staff at Thonburi Bamrungmuang Hospital. They are so cheerful and helpful; they even stand by the elevator, press the button, and constantly ask if I need anything. It's amazing! …Finally, I want to say that for anyone deciding whether or not to get LASIK, I highly recommend Dr. Namphueng. Let me tell you, it's great! If you have the money, just do it. Plus, the hospital offers installment payments via credit card, which is amazing! And another thing, the femto technique I had done is currently at a really good price. It even includes a free night's stay at the hospital! It's totally worth it because after the procedure, you only need to come back for a check-up the next day, so it's super convenient. You just wake up and go straight down for your check-up without having to travel. It's especially easy if you're traveling alone (but it's better if you have someone with you). The rooms are also great and very clean. Check out the admin and their current promotions. (I had mine done in February 2026)
0x30e299f132eaa2c5_0x1a8f1c74d5ee1fb3.author: Pimmy Makeup

0x30e299f132eaa2c5_0x1a8f1c74d5ee1fb3.text: The story is that I've been nearsighted since the first year of high school, so I've worn glasses ever since, and contact lenses occasionally. Around the fourth year of high school, a friend got LASIK surgery. She told me about it, and it was terrifying! The machine was making loud noises, the lights would disappear while she was looking, and all sorts of other problems (90s technology, you know, so it must have been as scary as she described). I wanted to do it too. At first, I planned to ask my parents, but I was afraid of going blind. I'm not handsome, and if I went blind, would I even be able to find a wife? So I put it off and just wore glasses and contact lenses ever since. Time flew by… Then, three years ago, Som got it done. When she came back, she asked me again, "How was it?" This time, the plot changed! There were no loud banging noises, the machine was very quiet, and it didn't hurt at all. So I got motivated again. I wanted to do it, but asking my parents for money wasn't an option anymore. I had to work and save up, scrimping and ditching. But by the time I saved enough, I needed lenses, a flash, a light… everything went wrong. So I started researching again. Actually, I was going to do it before I went to the Koh Larn Trail photoshoot. But I was afraid of going to the beach because of the strong sun and dust, plus riding a motorbike, and after Koh Larn I had a packed schedule with no free time. I asked the doctor, and they said it was possible, but to be careful of sweat getting in my eyes. I sweat a lot, so I postponed it. I finally got an appointment yesterday with Dr. Namphueng for LASIK double eyelid surgery. There was a discount promotion, and it included a room in the hospital. After booking, I drove there alone. When I arrived at the Thonburi Bamrungmuang LASIK Center by ACRS, I registered and had a preliminary eye exam. I wasn't nervous yet while waiting to see the doctor. When the doctor came, she did a detailed eye test. I also have farsightedness. The doctor let me choose whether to remove all the grafts or leave some for reading. I chose to remove them all. So, I opted for femto. While waiting for the procedure, I started to get nervous. They alternated between anesthetic and antibiotic eye drops. When it was time to go under the knife, I lay down. The doctor and nurse were very calm. They explained every step. "Open the corneal flap," they said. "Look at the light, the instrument will block your view. Look at the light, 3, 2, 1, done!" They said. I rested for a bit, then they did the other eye until it was finished. I thought to myself, "Wow, I was just scared for nothing. There was nothing to be afraid of." I went up to my room, took my medicine, and slept from the afternoon until morning, waking up and falling asleep intermittently. When I woke up in the morning, I washed my eyes as the doctor recommended, took a shower, and then stood looking out the window. The first thing I saw was... I could see Wat Phra Kaew (Temple of the Emerald Buddha) so clearly with my own eyes! I wish I had done this sooner. I just went to the doctor to check the wound; everything's fine. There's still some irritation, but the doctor said to use artificial tears frequently. I can drive home now. In short, I should have done this a long time ago. If anyone is considering it, I highly recommend it. It's not as scary as you think. In short #2, I can finally wear my sunglasses that I've been collecting!
0x30e299f132eaa2c5_0x1a8f1c74d5ee1fb3.author: RUNPIX

0x30e299f132eaa2c5_0x1a8f1c74d5ee1fb3.text: 👀🫰🏼 New Eyes Near Me ❤️ 🎉 Review of LASIK Surgery for New Eyes Near Me I had Femto LASIK surgery at Thonburi Bamrungmuang Hospital with Dr. Namphueng. She's very kind, friendly, and lovely. 👁️ First, I had a consultation with the doctor, but the procedure couldn't be done because I had an infection and clouding in both eyes, so I had to recover for a week. 👁️ The following week, I went to see the doctor, feeling incredibly anxious about whether I could have the surgery. Finally, the doctor said I could, so I decided to go ahead with it immediately. 💕 The doctor was so kind and gave me the option of a razor-blade procedure, which might save money, but I was already set on Femto LASIK. 👁️ When it was time for the procedure, the doctor was very kind and explained everything that would be done. When the laser was fired, I smelled burning, as they say, but I didn't feel any pain because they used a lot of anesthetic. After the procedure, the doctor checked my eyes and took me to my room. 💕 This package included a one-night stay. In the room, my sister was there to keep me company, which was great. Everything was complete, the room was clean, and I slept comfortably. The nurses were very attentive and caring. 💕 My boyfriend brought me food and drinks, which was great. 👁️ In the first few days after the procedure, my eyes hurt, and when I slept, my eyes would tear up a lot, causing a burning sensation on both the left and right sides alternately. I couldn't open my eyes, even though the doctor told me to rest for 6 hours. I kept waking up even after taking the sleeping pills the doctor gave me. 👁️ When I woke up the next morning, my vision started to clear up, and I could see on my own again. This time, the doctor had me wear sunglasses for another eye checkup, and then I was able to go home. ❤️ In summary, if anyone is considering LASIK surgery, I recommend Dr. Namphueng. She's lovely, friendly, and I was very impressed. I also recommend Thonburi Bamrungmuang Hospital; it's clean, luxurious, and not expensive. ❤️ Finally, I want to thank all my friends and family for their support and for taking such good care of me throughout the procedure and my hospital stay. ❤️ Thank you to my sister for taking such good care of me. ❤️ Thank you to my husband for paying for it so I could see a new world, and for buying me food and drinks. ❤️ Thank you to myself for having the courage to do it and for opening my heart to this new pair of eyes. It's amazing! 🙏🏻 I apologize if I haven't replied to everyone, but thank you for all the encouragement. 0x30e299f132eaa2c5_0x1a8f1c74d5ee1fb3.text: Review of LASIK and ICL Implant at Thonburi Bamrungmuang LASIK Center by Dr. Namphueng (ACRS) Left Eye: Femto LASIK -7.75 diopters, -4.00 diopters Right Eye: ICL -13.50 diopters, -3.50 diopters I was very impressed with Dr. Namphueng and I am grateful for her excellent care from the first consultation and decision to have LASIK. It was a very good decision. Before the surgery, my vision was already blurry; it felt like I was only using my left eye, while my right eye couldn't see anything at all, only close up. I could barely see signs while driving. So I decided I should get LASIK. However, because of my high prescription, most doctors recommended ICL implants, so I waited because I was scared. Then I consulted with Dr. Namphueng and finally got treatment. They explained that my left eye could have Femto LASIK with full diopter, although some refractive error might remain, but my right eye needed ICL. I decided to go ahead with it because of the thorough explanation and information. Initially, I was very scared about the eye that needed the ICL implant, especially after watching videos of the procedure. On the day of the surgery, I requested additional local anesthesia for peace of mind (normally it's not necessary). The procedure itself wasn't scary at all. The doctor explained every step. I only felt something pushing against my eye. It was over in less than 15 minutes. Then I moved to another room for the Femto LASIK surgery on the other eye. I just lay still and looked at the green lights above me. The doctor and nurses told me to stay still for only 20 seconds, and it was done. This felt much easier than the lens implant surgery. Everything was done. Dr. Namphueng and the nurses did an excellent job. I was very impressed. Afterwards, they had me stay overnight. The rooms and the nurses at this hospital were excellent, much better than many other hospitals. They were very kind. One day after the surgery, my vision was somewhat clear, with some blurriness. I didn't feel any pain, just some tightness in the eye that had the ICL surgery, and some dryness in the Femto eye. I was even able to drive myself home, which was great. Seven days after the surgery, my vision gradually improved. Sometimes it was clear, sometimes slightly blurry, but nothing abnormal. Post-operative care was simple: just use the eye drops as prescribed by the doctor, avoid washing your hair, and prevent activities that cause sweating. Also, keep water out of your eyes. **Highly recommended for anyone interested in LASIK surgery. The doctor is excellent, 10/10.**

0x30e299f132eaa2c5_0x1a8f1c74d5ee1fb3.text: Happy Birthday to me! 🎂🎂 This year, I gifted myself LASIK surgery to say goodbye to my glasses. This year has brought many changes in my life, but what remains is my warm family, my supportive sister, my lovely friends, my demanding but stable job, and now my wonderful husband and his family. May this year be filled with happiness for me and my family, may my parents be healthy, may my savings increase, and may my shifts be smooth and not exhausting. 🙏🙏🏻 Review of my birthday gift: “New eyesight, closer to me!” 12 years of wearing glasses and 3 years of deciding to get LASIK. I was about to insert a tube in a patient when sweat got into my eyes. I couldn't wipe it off because it was on my glasses, they kept falling off, and my eyes stung and tears streamed down my cheeks. After the doctor finished inserting the tube, I rushed to wipe the sweat off, feeling very frustrated because it was an emergency situation. I started researching LASIK, looking for hospitals where people I knew had it done, and reading reviews about the pros and cons. Everyone said the benefits outweighed the drawbacks; it makes life easier because you don't have to wear glasses, although you might experience dry eyes sometimes, which can be helped by artificial tears. Because of my fear, I wasn't brave enough to get it done yet. I kept reading reviews and checking out different hospitals until today. Okay!! I don't want to wear glasses anymore. At work, I won't have to worry about sweat getting in my eyes and not being able to wipe them clean. This year, another problem arose: when my husband kisses me, my glasses get scratched, so I have to wipe them clean constantly. So, I decided to just do it. I'd read reviews and researched quite a bit. Dr. Namphueng, Dr. Suthanee Sorthirathi, is a skilled doctor with many reviews. But… on the day of the procedure, I was still scared. My eyes… eye procedures are scary! 😂 But the doctor explained everything from the initial eye exam to the completion of the procedure, including post-procedure care. Everything was explained in an easy-to-understand way, which reduced my fear. After the procedure, I took Paracetamol and Diazepam and slept for about 5 hours. When I woke up, my eyes were crystal clear! My new eyesight is truly near-perfect. Bye-bye, Paphat's glasses! 👐🏻❤️💕

0x30e299f132eaa2c5_0x1a8f1c74d5ee1fb3.text: Hello! Today, I'd like to share my own fresh and up-to-date LASIK experience (surgery on December 4th) at Thonburi Bamrungmuang Hospital with Dr. (Ph.D.), Asst. Prof. Dr. Theerathep Tantayakom. I have to say... I was absolutely impressed from start to finish. ❤️ Previously, I was extremely nearsighted, with a thin cornea. Plus, I spent a lot of time at the computer due to work. I experienced flashes of light for a while, which led me to a very thorough eye exam. And that's when I met Dr. Theerathep. The doctor had me treat my corneal ruptures first (both eyes 😭). He didn't rush me to have surgery, saying, "Let your eyes be strong first. Safety is more important." I really liked that. He took me step by step, didn't push me on packages, and didn't push me on anything. After the procedure, he started his LASIK assessment. The pre-surgery exam was incredibly thorough, detailing everything from corneal thickness, curvature, and dry eye level. The doctor also explained in a very easy-to-understand way that there are many techniques, including Femto, PRK, and ReLEx. There's not just one type of LASIK, as many people think. Femto was a good choice for me because my cornea is quite thin and I use the computer a lot. The doctor said it was the safest option for my eyes and emphasized "safety over clarity." I felt like he was choosing based on my true eye condition, not trying to sell me anything. I was surprised when I entered the surgery room. It wasn't scary at all. The doctor had a very gentle hand, constantly saying, "Just one more step," "Easy, easy, easy," and really helped me relax. It was so quick, I didn't even have time to think about it. 😂 After the procedure, my vision was immediately clearer, about 70–80%. It felt like HD vision, but there was some fog, which the nurse said was normal. He explained in great detail what eye drops to use, when to use them, what to do and what not to do, and how to rest my eyes to reduce dryness in the early stages. Overall, it was really great. The doctors, nurses, and all the staff were friendly and caring. For anyone who's hesitant, I can tell you that LASIK isn't as scary as you think. If you're looking for a truly thorough examination, considering your true eye condition, and not pushy sales pitches, this hospital is the best! ✨❤️

0x3102bf25de0dfd2f_0x2a85782a1182f7ad.text: I started researching online from various sources until I found reviews about this Pattaya LASIK center, which was known for its specialized expertise. I contacted them and found them responsive and regularly updated with information, so I decided to go with them. 1. The first step is an eye examination, costing approximately 1500 baht. The doctor will then assess whether your eyes are suitable for the procedure. “We don’t make the decision ourselves, that’s important!” 2. If the doctor determines that you are suitable, they will inform you of the procedure and cost, and schedule a surgery date. 3. On the day of the surgery, your face and eye area are sterilized before the procedure. It was a very unique experience for me – just looking at green and red lights for less than 5 minutes. It wasn't painful, just exciting and surprising that it was already over! 4. After the procedure, you can see immediately, but you should close your eyes frequently to aid healing and prevent infection, as advised by the doctor. 5. Follow-up appointments are scheduled for 1 day, 7 days, 1 month, 3 months, and 6 months, including eye drops as prescribed. *During the first 7 days, I experienced sensitivity to bright light, eye fatigue, and light scattering. However, this improved after that period. The only issue is occasional glare at night; it doesn't make life that difficult. Overall, I'm very satisfied with the results. 6. I didn't receive any benefits; I'm just someone who wanted to share information in case others wanted to try it. My prescription was -350-400. After the procedure, I no longer need glasses. I can swim and play sports freely. I'm 25 years old, which makes me want to try many more things in life. Consider it yourself: consult a doctor, save money, and set goals.

0x3102bf25de0dfd2f_0x2a85782a1182f7ad.text: I lived in Löbau, Germany until 1.5 years ago and had cataract surgery. Now I'm in Pattaya, Thailand. After the surgery, I was extremely sensitive to light. In the evenings and in supermarkets, LED lights in particular caused me to see blurry lines and an aura around the light source. I could only see distant objects as if through a fog. It was very distressing. Then I read about YAG laser treatment. They dilate the pupils with drops, and then the laser is applied to the eye. After 24 hours, I can see clearly again, I have no more blurry vision, and no more aura around light sources in the dark. It's wonderful! I just wonder: WHY DIDN'T I HAVE THIS DONE SOONER? The total cost was about 13,000 baht, using the latest technology from Zeiss. Thank you to the whole team and the doctor. Very professional! Unfortunately, I had already been to the same hospital in Bangkok a year ago. Two nights of extreme abdominal pain (antibiotic overdose) cost well over 200,000 baht. Against medical advice, I discharged myself because I didn't want to spend any more money and was feeling somewhat better. When it came time to pay for the eye surgery, they seriously claimed I still owed 40,000 baht?! I explained that I had discontinued the treatment because I wasn't prepared to pay that exact amount if I were to continue. I specifically confirmed with the treating physician that everything was paid for and completed, and that my medication was already included in the final payment. Disappointingly, even though it had been clarified and agreed upon, I was left feeling like someone who hadn't paid their bill. Annoying, but it seems that discrepancies frequently occur there.

I recommend Already trusting Dr Tapasit for some years for my wreck damaged teeth. Recently had a difficult extraction to do on a molar tooth with the root only remaining to extract. Was done in less than 10 minutes without pain and difficulties though it is usually a difficult task to perform. Special care is brought by the team to avoid the pain. Even they use local gum anesthetic before doing main injection !! Prices are quite fair, especially for big jobs (implants, etc..) and there is no cheating : I normally had to set up 2 implants and some bone adding...but it finally ended with only one implant as the space between teeth was not enough to set up 2 implants. Dr Tapasit speaks a perfect English, so communication is quite easy and he is really pleasant to deal with. I highly recommend Adenza dental, especially for foreigners who are usually quite demanding.

Dr. Tapasit is a professional, skilled and very personable dentist who was trained in the United States at Georgetown University. His Pattaya practice is a cut above the rest and definitely state-of-the art. Both his parents are physicians and he speaks perfect English since he was raised in the US from age 9, returning to Thailand 25 years later. While he could, no doubt, be a top tier dentist in any wealthy American city, he has (like many of us) opted for a less stressful life in Thailand where he has raised a family with his Thai wife. If you are an expat American, Aussie or Brit, Dr. Tapasit is definitely someone that you will feel comfortable with and you will likely make Dr. Tapasit your dentist, just as I have done.

0x310295fd3e3c682b_0xda32ff6e6dc9173b.text: I want to give this clinic's doctor a good review. The mole on the bottom right corner had been treated with laser in China once, which was basically ineffective. I came to this clinic last October for treatment; the price was 2500 baht for two moles. The mole on the bottom right corner was almost completely gone after one treatment. As you can see in the picture, it was due to hair growing from a follicle and some small amount of gray pigment deposition. Overall, I'm very satisfied; the mole is now smooth. The mole on the top left corner was almost completely removed after one treatment, but there was still a tiny bit left. I had it treated a second time in January. The doctor didn't penetrate too deeply with the laser to avoid scarring, but a very small spot still remained. Today was my second touch-up treatment. This time, the doctor increased the laser intensity and told me that if it wasn't completely removed, surgical removal might be necessary. I won't do it again this time, regardless of whether it's completely removed or not, because I'm generally satisfied. The last two laser treatments were free. The doctor is an elderly gentleman who only sees patients for a total of 4 hours each day, in the morning and afternoon, so remember to make an appointment in advance if you want to see him.

0x3050318f53e771bd_0xb9884a958ae075d8.text: Had an infection on my hand, I was on antibiotics from a local pharmacy, but after a few days the wound still didn't look great so I decided to come here. Staff were very helpful, everyone spoken enough English that the process was clear and easy. Arrived on Monday at 11:00AM, was promptly seen for paperwork and then a nurse for initial assessment. Total wait time of 5 or 10 minutes. They scheduled an appointment for the same day at 2:00pm with a doctor. At 2:00 I was seen immediately by the doctor! I was amazed that a big busy hospital like this was on time with appointments. The doctor wanted to get a tissue sample, so I went to another room and waited for a bit while things were prepared. The doctor came in, cleaned the wound and took a sample. I told the doctor I didn't want freezing as the wound didn't really hurt, and he listened and respected my choice. I then waited about 20 minutes for the test results, and they came back negative, nothing to worry about. Can't recommend this place enough to travellers! It would have been easier for them to just give me some mega dose of antibiotics and send me on my way (and they could have made more money off me). But they took their time, did it right, and were very professional. And all said and done total cost: only 1500 Bhat! Can't beat that. Amazing service.

0x30e29b8c64d5fe77_0x160fcd8d81add07d.text: I happened to have to make two visits to Bang Po Hospital. Four or five years ago, I broke my left foot. I was staying in the Saphan Kwai district, close to Bang Po. My foot was X-rayed, I was shown the cracked bone and the orthopedic surgeon advised me to wear a special shoe and keep my feet up for two weeks. He and the nurses and staff were very professional and able. Two years ago, I developed a bad infection in my right elbow. It hardened like stone and started to spread down to my hand and up to my shoulder. Again, I went to Bang Po Hospital. They admitted me and the admitting doctor wan another orthopedic surgeon. It turned out I had MRSA, myocin resistant staph infection. Luckily, my surgeon opened my elbow and cleared out as much of the infectious material in my elbow that he could reach. It took awhile but I was OK. The charges for both trips were staggeringly cheap. With MRSA, I had a private room for a week, outpatient for a week, surgery, prescription meds, etc. and it was about $2,000 US. I cannot recommend this hospital strongly enough!

0x30da3bd9c28f7ddf_0xeea6f730ea1f9c9f.text: I arrived at Embrace after three months in a primary treatment facility. Not quite sure of how to integrate back into life and still needing support it was an easy choice to make as the next step in my recovery journey. Embrace came very highly recommended and is leading in the field of secondary treatments, upon my own queries the program and structure was exactly what I was looking for. I stayed with embrace for 5 months, going through the program too the best of my ability, which was up and down there were good days and bad yet throughout I never felt pressured to do or be anything other than what I was capable of and most of all I felt completely supported. The therapeutic program is perfectly rounded three days of the week contain informative groups led by experts in the field of addiction, mental health and personal growth. Alternate days there are community activities ranging from hikes in the mountains of Chiang Mai to painting classes in the ancient temples in the Old City. I also particularly loved the water park and go karting. Whilst there is always something to do with the community, you are never forced, I found sometimes I would need some personal space for me this was an opportunity to explore the area on one of the provided bikes or simply go and get a relaxing massage to unwind. A huge shout out to my counsellor at Embrace Eléonore King who I still work with to this day giving me such amazing insight on anxiety, fear, self discovery and a new lens on who I am and what I am capable of. Whilst at Embrace I was solely able to focus on my next steps in recovery, I planned my goals with my recovery coach Phil who guided me amazingly throughout my time, sharing his own experiences to best equip me in my own journey. I worked on my fitness with Dan Sully who leads personal boxing classes and is an amazing human being. Dan Noble was also an amazing support to me when ever I was not 100% he was always around to lend an ear and mentorship. I wouldn't have been able stay in the country if it hadn't been for Mark C. the seamless transitions of boarder runs and organising trips to immigration was a luxury which really is appreciated. All of the staff at embrace made me feel safe, supported and cared for. I genuinely felt like I was coming back home at the end of each day. Henk and Bill run a very professional program. They are dedicated to each and every person who comes through the doors at embrace. This is evident to me since leaving, Embrace has maintained regular communication and continued to support me on my journey. I cannot make assumptions on where I might be if I hadn't spent these 5 months at Embrace, I can however say I would never of had the opportunity that I have now, the structure and routine in my life, the deep personal understanding and most importantly to me the connection with myself and others in this tight nit community that Embrace creates. I thank each and every person at embrace. I can not speak highly enough for what this place has done for my life.
0x30da3bd9c28f7ddf_0xeea6f730ea1f9c9f.author: Jack McPherson

0x30da3bd9c28f7ddf_0xeea6f730ea1f9c9f.text: I didn't know what to expect upon arriving at Embrace. I needed secondary treatment after primary. All I knew was I needed a safe environment... Embrace offered me that safe environment plus so much more. I met some amazing people... the staff... incredibly supportive and knowledgeable. Seeing things in myself that I couldn't see. I've been to other sober houses in the past but what puts Embrace ahead of the rest is the attention given to my behaviors, my growth and my recovery. Gently pushed and motivated to try new things, to get out of my comfort zone into the 'growth zone'.. The support i received at Embrace during early recovery allowed me the time and space to get to know myself... to learn who I am in recovery. I didn't feel like a number... I felt a part of a family. I was surrounded by healthy people serious about their recovery and that energy rubbed off on me. That is what Embrace is. A family, a community of people striving for personal growth and helping each other along the way. The extended community beyond Embrace was not something i was expecting. Ex-clients and people connected to Embrace through strong recovery and community coming to the Embrace BBQ every Sunday and helping me see that not only recovery was possible but that I could be apart of something.... It gave me that sense of belonging i needed. There's no opportunity to get bored at Embrace... Every day there are activities ranging from Football games, cooking classes, onsite yoga sessions, art groups, badminton, ping pong tournaments, excursions, soundbowl healing, Buddhism teaching classes, onsite quizzes, hikes, bike rides, go-karting, kayaking, bootcamps, CrossFit, amazing markets and so much more. The location offers lovely mountain views, quiet surroundings but not far from shopping malls and amazing restaurants... There is a wide variety of counselors available as well. Each with their own skillset and so approachable.. I feel like i was spoilt for choice. Embrace goes to any length to ensure clients are comfortable and settled. If i had a problem i never felt like my concerns or requests fell on deaf ears. Not once. I found myself at Embrace. I cant recommend them highly enough. Thank you Embrace.
0x30da3bd9c28f7ddf_0xeea6f730ea1f9c9f.author: Chris

0x30da3bd9c28f7ddf_0xeea6f730ea1f9c9f.text: I went to Embrace Sober House in the beautiful Chiang Mai in July after completing three months primary treatment. My intentions were to go to a sober living environment and get used to going to NA meetings before I came back to Australia, but I got a lot more then I was hoping for They organised transport to and from the meetings, had a well structured program to keep you busy in recovery with an abundance of exercise activities ( my favourite being the trail walking with Henk, I found my new healthy hobbie thanks to Embrace) , guided meditation, a great selection of counselors and group therapist and not to mention the support workers who were alwàys around to keep us happy and keep us safe. There was frequent drug and alcohol testing in the facility, I think this is a must in a sober house. As good as the Thai food was I made and option to cook my own food most of the time and they provide a huge kitchen with everything you will every need. I left Embrace with around 25 NA meetings under my belt in a month and some great connections within the NA community. I would recommend Embrace to anyone who is serious about recovery and wants NA as apart of there program when they leave. If your curious whether Embrace is for you, why not head over and check it out, Henk will take you on a tour show you just how good the place is. My room felt like a 5 🌟 hotel, and the property is absolutely beautiful. Thanks to all the staff and fellow clients at Embrace you made my stay well worth the money. Thank you I attached a photo of myself on the home stretch of a 24km trail walk/run with sully who is the fitness coach at embrace. This trail had over 1000m elevation and was probably one of the best days of my life.
0x30da3bd9c28f7ddf_0xeea6f730ea1f9c9f.author: Mase

0x30da3bd9c28f7ddf_0xeea6f730ea1f9c9f.text: My son was in Embrace from July 2022 and all the support help and advice that he got from the team there is the best that one would expect for their son. We are a small family and unfortunately my son was suffering with addiction of drugs and alcohol. We seeked advice from others and found that Embrace is the right place for him. The support that he got from the staff and the counselling staff helping him through his journey with his recovery was to a very high standard. We have always had a very good rapport with all the staff and they were very supportive and helpful and our communication was very good and they went out to all lengths to help us and keep us posted about our son’s progress. We cannot thank Embrace enough again for all the support and encouragement that they have given to both my son and for my family. I would like to add that my son is doing very well towards his recovery and has found employment nearby and still has the support of Embrace for any problems that he might encounter in his recovery We as a family from England are very grateful to Embrace and their entire team. Unfortunately I will not name any names in a review but you know who you are and thank you all very much again. If you have got anyone who was in my son’s condition I have no reservations but to recommend that they come to Embrace and get all the help and professional support and we highly recommend this facility for anyone. We are very happy with the care support and help that they have given to not only my son but to my entire family.
0x30da3bd9c28f7ddf_0xeea6f730ea1f9c9f.author: Malkeet Saini

0x30da3bd9c28f7ddf_0xeea6f730ea1f9c9f.text: I am a parent of an addict who was a client of Embrace Sober House. My son has been an addict for over 15 years and has sought treatment on numerous occasions without the success he has now achieved at Embrace Sober House. If you find yourself in the same position as I then you need to get them admitted to this amazing facility. The Staff are amazing and extremely supportive, nothing is too much trouble to them, there is always someone on hand if you need anything from Counsellors, Recovery Coaches, Fitness Coaches & volunteers. Most of the people there have been on this journey themselves and I believe this gives them the insight required to help the clients achieve their goal of life without substance abuse. The premises are outstanding, fabulous atmosphere, great accommodations and beautiful location. A big shout out to Henk - a huge success story and now the owner of Embrace with Bill. They both helped my son enormously, I can't thank them enough - I got my boy back. As a parent we all want our children to be happy and fulfilled - my son can now see a future without drugs, is living a happy, busy and fruitful life. Words are really not enough to express the feeling of joy I feel seeing him loving life. Embrace is an oasis for anyone suffering from addiction of any kind. Let them help you.....
0x30da3bd9c28f7ddf_0xeea6f730ea1f9c9f.author: Jan Pike

0x30da3bd9c28f7ddf_0xeea6f730ea1f9c9f.text: My stay at Embrace was truly life changing. Travelling from London by myself in my 50s was so daunting but all completely worth it. I was met at the airport with such a warm welcome. My room was sooooo lovely and spacious. I particularly enjoyed the fun-packed schedule and I always had a choice to join every day. Which I did because I didn’t want to miss anything they offered. I liked the family community feeling of the place and the group really felt like a real support network. The community had all shared experiences and were free of addiction and truly enjoying life. We done so much together, cycling, visiting temples, elephants, Muay Thai, yoga, swimming, bamboo rafting, gorgeous meals out and cooking meals together, meditation, AA and NA, massage, barbecues, chess, hiking, shopping, markets and so much more. I really loved the staff. The therapy counsellors and recovery coach were real quality and delivered very educational sessions. I found out a lot about how my mind ticks. I haven’t laughed so much in years. I actually didn’t want to leave. I could have lived there forever, but the experience Embrace gave me was the tools to thrive back in my own life. I will definitely keep returning though. I am absolutely in love with Chiang Mai. It will always have a place in my heart.
0x30da3bd9c28f7ddf_0xeea6f730ea1f9c9f.author: L

0x30da3bd9c28f7ddf_0xeea6f730ea1f9c9f.text: Embrace is a wonderful place which really helped me with my recovery and got me back on the right path to a fit Healthy lifestyle. I would highly recommend Embrace to any one looking for help with any sort of addiction and secondary treatment. The staff were all very supportive and helpful with great skills in battling addiction that they are more than willing to share also an interview to pair you with the right councilor to suit you and your needs which I thought was great I really enjoyed the conciling and got alot out of it. Morning group sessions with all the other clients and a councilor with everyone checking in and helping each other out was a great experience. They have great on site facilities gym, kitchen , meditation , and swimming pool. They provide transportation to 5 star gym facilities swimming pools, massages , hikes ,nature walks and meetings with a weekly excursion . I really enjoyed the fitness and gym side of recovery leaving with some new personal bests in the gym which I was so excited about. For me Embrace was a five star experience thanks to all that helped me along my journey and prepared me for my return to the outside world. I will be forever grateful 🙏 😊 Below is photos of my room a photo of my gains from the gym and a trip to the water fall hike.
0x30da3bd9c28f7ddf_0xeea6f730ea1f9c9f.author: Hamish

0x30da3bd9c28f7ddf_0xeea6f730ea1f9c9f.text: Embrace changed my life, 4 years into sobriety! I found myself backsliding after a series of challenges in the past year, was losing control yet becoming more controlling than ever, a dry drunk. To the point of a physical/mental/emotional breakdown. Fortunately, somehow, I realized I was in trouble and managed to get in touch with Henk after a suggestion from a mutual friend. Henk and the staff at Embrace met with me and showed me their program and facility. I instantly felt relief, I knew this was what I needed to do and the place I needed to be. The combination of responsible freedom and the ability to tailor my recovery process to my needs, with a great variety of counselling staff, recovery coaches, mindfulness, and group sessions, got me back on my feet. Personally I took advantage of extra available counselling sessions with my counsellors of choice in 1on1 recovery, personal, and mindfulness. It really helped me get back to my core values and problems I’d lost sight of with the craziness of life, and after some years in the outside world, it revealed some new character defects to work on. All said, the best decision of my sober life, getting help before I drank again wasn’t where I wanted to be but so incredibly grateful for Embrace for being there before I did!

0x3102be6ca7050e71_0x1600a93877191c50.text: 🩺 How a Thai doctor saved me from pain that they couldn't cure in Russia: The story began long before Thailand. Back in Russia, I felt a strange, nagging pain in my right upper quadrant. It was alarming, especially as I was preparing to move. I was seriously scared, feared the worst, and went for a full checkup. I donated blood. Had an ultrasound. Swallowed a tube with a camera. Everything was fine. The only thing they found was Helicobacter pylori bacteria in my stomach lining. I was prescribed a course of antibiotics. I took everything exactly as prescribed, but the pain didn't go away. It would subside, then return. Then one day in Thailand, this time in Pattaya, I felt a sharp cramp again. I decided to go to a Thai clinic in the hopes of finally figuring out what was going on. My insurance didn't cover routine visits—only emergency ones. I knew that if I went to a private hospital like Bangkok Hospital, I'd shell out at least 10,000 baht just for the appointment and the pills. So the choice was obvious. I went to the public clinic, Banglamung Hospital, where my friend had gotten an X-ray, a cast, and all the necessary medications for a mere 1,700 baht when he broke his arm. But this time, when I went in person, I had no idea what to do. The ticket machine wasn't working. The display was blank. Everything was in Thai. I stood there, lost in the middle of the hall, wondering where to go or who to see. Luckily, a Thai woman waiting in line with her son helped me. I told her what was bothering me. She went to find out which doctor I needed to see and returned with the news: the doctor I needed was no longer available that day. But she told me that the same doctor was available after work at a private clinic—literally a five-minute walk away. I decided to go there, got a number, and waited until it opened. It was my first visit to such a small Thai clinic. And, frankly, I was amazed by the atmosphere. The strawberry-colored wooden ottomans at the entrance—it was like something out of a fairy tale. And inside, everything was very simple, cozy, and cozy. The doctor looked me in the eyes, listened carefully, gently touched my stomach—and that was it. No tests, no ultrasound. He said I had a gallbladder spasm. Apparently, it was caused by nerves. He prescribed two medications—and that was it. I took a two-week course, and the pain went away forever. I was amazed then at how accurately the doctor diagnosed me without any equipment. Just from experience. In Russia, I had undergone countless tests, wasted time and money—but no one could figure out the cause of the pain. And here, they simply helped me… by feeling my stomach with their hands. I'm not saying in any way that our doctors are worse. Russian medicine has saved me more than once in the most difficult situations. Something just went wrong this time. And what's surprising is that I paid pennies for the clinic appointment. It was such a small amount that I don't even remember it. What is treated (translated from the clinic window): General appointments and conditions: • Consultations on age-related changes • Headaches, migraines, headaches • Weakness, chronic fatigue • Decreased immunity Cardiovascular system: • Blood clots, circulatory disorders • High cholesterol • High blood pressure • Heart disease • Arrhythmia Gastrointestinal tract and metabolism: • Heartburn, belching, gastritis • Acidity imbalance • Elevated enzymes • Poor digestion • Liver disease • Constipation, diarrhea • Bloating • Diabetes Respiratory system and allergies: • Chronic cough • Runny nose, sinusitis • Allergies • Shortness of breath • Bronchitis • Asthma • COPD Skin and joints: • Skin Inflammations • Psoriasis • Eczema • Fungus • Herpes • Arthritis • Gout • Rheumatism • Osteoarthritis Neurology and Vascular Services: • Weakness in the Limbs • Post-Stroke Conditions • Impaired Blood Flow • Numbness • Seizures • Paresis Other Services: • HIV • Immunodeficiencies • Supportive Therapy • Chronic Disease Management • Nutrition and Supplement Consultations • Vitamin Selection Vaccinations: – Flu – Tetanus – Rabies – Hepatitis A and B – HPV (Cervical Cancer) – Pneumococcal (Lung Vaccine) – Measles, Rubella, Mumps – and others

0x3102bdb2018f4ca7_0x7e0cc0997094a6dd.text: I recently moved to Pattaya about a year ago, and the clinic accepts the Gold Card (government health insurance). When I actually met Mint at the clinic, she was incredibly lovely – polite, cheerful, and answered all my questions. She helped me a lot, significantly reducing my anxiety about visiting the dentist. This was a truly positive first impression. I sincerely commend them! 🙂 Although it's a small clinic, the equipment, tools, and atmosphere are all clean and tidy. There's a spacious waiting area for both patients and their families, and a clean restroom. Dr. Pongsakorn, the clinic's resident dentist, is also incredibly kind, patient, polite, and speaks very nicely. He helped break down my fears, providing excellent guidance at every step, explaining what I was doing and what would happen next. This greatly reduced my anxiety and nervousness. Plus, he has a gentle touch; I barely felt any pain. And he's excellent at English! I brought my foreign husband to get dental work done here again, and we were still very impressed. We plan to have regular dental care at The H Smile in the future. 😊 A truly heartfelt thank you for the excellent service from Dr. Pongsakorn, all the assistants, and especially Mint, the receptionist. 🙏 I would highly recommend Dr. Pongsakorn to anyone reading this honest review. He is a truly excellent dentist and very trustworthy. 👍

Booking: Very easy. Just call the number from Google Maps, mention you're using your Gold Card, and schedule an appointment for a date and time that suits you. (But it's probably difficult now because it's likely much busier.) The dental experience: The atmosphere during the teeth cleaning wasn't bad; it wasn't uncomfortable. The dentist was very nice, kind, and spoke politely (though he was a little heavy-handed because he was a man). The assistant nurse was also very helpful, making the procedure go smoothly. Interior: Clean and comfortable. There are large, soft leather sofas to sit on, and they provide extra chairs if needed. There's a large TV screen showing things to watch while waiting. 0x30e29e987b7ff7f3_0xea57c8cf4d9eb722.text: Walk-ins are welcome before 10:00 AM for free sterilization; no appointment is needed. There are cancellations every day. While appointments are limited to 50 animals per day, on the day we went, only about 20 animals were actually sterilized. Cancellation surgeries start at 10:00 AM, and patients can go home by 11:00 AM. Open Monday to Friday, closed on public holidays. Remember to withhold food and water from your cat or dog for 12 hours before surgery. Register before 10:00 AM and remember to keep track of the queue to ensure it's within the 50 slots available. This prevents staff from miscounting and claiming it's full, so you can dispute the scheduling. Please bring your ID card (one ID card per two cats or dogs).
0x30e29e987b7ff7f3_0xea57c8cf4d9eb722.author: Parepimuk Wuti

0x30e29fae86ddbf77_0x536d890b9c80faae.text: Had the pleasure of staying at Unit 7A, the top floor of the building - a quiet, convenient spot right in the heart of Silom. The location is perfect... just steps from Chong Nonsi BTS, and walkable to Sala Daeng BTS, Silom MRT, and also Dusit Central Park mall. The view was fantastic, surrounded by iconic tall buildings yet not blocked by them. You still get a sense of openness, especially at sunrise and sunset. There’s no noise from clubs or bars at night, though you might still hear faint sounds of BTS trains in the distance. On weekdays, the Lalai Sap morning market comes alive right downstairs, full of friendly locals and affordable Thai food. It’s a lovely glimpse of everyday Bangkok life right at your doorstep. Laundry was easy too... there’s a washer on the ground floor and a rooftop area for drying clothes, which made longer stays really convenient. Overall, a great stay for anyone who wants easy city access without the chaos. Highly recommended.

0x311d7b0012e8fdc3_0xad31a4e9b8ddbf54.text: The dentist was incredibly gentle. The scraping was very clean and light; it didn't hurt at all. However, they were a bit late, 15 minutes late for my 10 am appointment, even though I was the first in line. But that's okay, it didn't hurt, so I forgive them. - Another thing I liked was how quickly they responded to my LINE message before they opened. Other clinics don't respond at all. And once they opened, they called back quickly, but I was even faster because I had already booked through LINE, haha. Basically, communication was incredibly easy. The best among all the dental clinics in this area in terms of easy communication and quick responses. - The counter staff looked a little grumpy, but it wasn't a big deal (just a slight contrast to the cheerful and friendly atmosphere on LINE, which was a bit stern at the counter; probably a different person than the admin). But they were polite and nothing else was bad. - The clinic looked clean, but there was a musty smell, probably from the mopping equipment. I recommend addressing the odor of the cleaning supplies. - But the main reason I'm deducting stars is the conversation of the assistants during the dental procedure. I'd like them to be more careful. The assistants were talking about Hlun Solo and laughing (especially at the beginning). And I had just been crying about Hlun Solo (actually, every day since he left). I've never met anyone who could talk about it so lightheartedly before. Luckily, the doctor eventually stopped it by saying something sad and changing the subject, so things gradually calmed down. The doctor just went along with it and didn't join in the gossip, which was very fortunate; otherwise, I think it would have escalated. It's best not to discuss sensitive topics like this in front of a third party. Choose your topics carefully, or if you do talk about it, do so respectfully towards the deceased and others. Tone of voice is important. I was so stressed during the procedure, wondering when we would talk about something else. But when we changed the subject to medical equipment, it was like heaven. - If I have the chance, I would go back again because the service was good, they responded quickly, scheduling was easy, and the price was reasonable. But I hope I won't encounter such inappropriate conversation again.

0x30e29faacfbf2beb_0x79c82f5d89716ac7.text: Visited on September 13, 2019. Among the many dentists in Bangkok, this is a well-known dentist with an established reputation among Japanese people. As a frequent visitor to many veterans who have lived in Bangkok for over 20 years, this dentist is a must-visit when it comes to reasonable treatment fees, quality of treatment, and the peace of mind of knowing they can communicate in Japanese. There may be better dentists in Bangkok, but this is my personal choice. Fluent Japanese is a challenge, but communication is sufficient with simple Japanese. If you encounter a dentist who doesn't speak Japanese, a Japanese-speaking staff member will act as an interpreter. However, since this is not an ultra-high-end dentist, you may be somewhat overwhelmed... But the peace of mind of having an interpreter, even if just for a brief moment, is great. I had a filling reattached to a missing tooth for 900 baht (3,200 yen), a full self-pay fee not covered by insurance. I also had tartar removed for the same 900 baht. I'm happy that simple treatments can be completed in a day.
0x30e29faacfbf2beb_0x79c82f5d89716ac7.author: dora dora

0x30e29faacfbf2beb_0x79c82f5d89716ac7.text: I had a ceramic filling on a broken molar treated here. The Japanese language support was also good when making an appointment, so I felt at ease. Dr. Pongsak treated me, and he spoke fluent Japanese. His treatment plan was easy to understand, and it almost felt like I was being treated at a Japanese dentist. The appointment took about 30 minutes, and the treatment was completed in one day, which I was very grateful for. The treatment cost 2,100 baht, but I don't think it's too expensive. The only downside is that it's a little far from the BTS station. It's closer from Thonglor. It's nice to be able to shop at Fuji Supermarket on the way back, though. As an aside, I was surprised to find that the man at the reception desk was fluent in Chinese (he was dealing with Chinese customers). He also seemed to speak English, so it seems like they can provide services in four languages.
0x30e29faacfbf2beb_0x79c82f5d89716ac7.author: yutaka sato

0x30e29faacfbf2beb_0x79c82f5d89716ac7.text: This dentist on Sukhumvit 49 is popular with many Japanese people. There are several dentists catering to Japanese people in Bangkok's Phrom Phong and Thonglor areas, but this is one of the more popular. When you call, you'll be surprised to hear, "Hello, this is the dentist..." but you can make an appointment in Japanese. It's not that the staff are rude, they just don't speak Japanese that well. They were fully booked for about a week, so I made an appointment for the earliest available date and time. The staff can also speak Japanese, so it's reassuring. I was worried the fees would be extremely high, but I was pleased that they weren't that expensive: 100 baht for the consultation, 1,500 baht for simple cavity treatment, and 1,500 baht for tartar removal.
0x30e29faacfbf2beb_0x79c82f5d89716ac7.author: JUN KOBA

0x30e29faacfbf2beb_0x79c82f5d89716ac7.text: Japanese OK I use this dentist. Japanese OK. They require an appointment, but if you're in pain and just pop in, they'll help you. When you call, they'll initially speak Thai, but if they realize you're speaking Japanese or Thai spoken by a Japanese person, they'll switch to Japanese. The dentists also speak Japanese, and a nurse will accompany you as an interpreter. In Thailand, a typical visit to the dentist is a one-time affair, but dental care is handled by specialized dentists, such as cavity treatment, anesthesia, and tooth extractions. Even if you pop in, if the dentist isn't there, you'll just get first-aid and have to go again. It's more expensive than a local dentist, but cheaper than a major private hospital. Insurance is accepted.

0x30da3ac3c51fb13b_0xf158e81c59acfafb.text: Highly recommend! Chotana Animal Hospital in Chiang Mai saved my dog's life. Their medical skills are excellent and their medical ethics are exemplary! Two years ago, my dog ​​was hit by a motorcycle and suffered severe bone displacement. At the time, we consulted several animal hospitals in Chiang Mai, and the answer was that they could only remove the fractured bone, meaning my dog ​​would be permanently disabled. This was heartbreaking. We didn't give up and continued searching for a clinic that could perform bone retraction and fixation (not just simple removal). Finally, our efforts paid off! We found Chotana Animal Hospital! After a thorough examination, the doctors here proposed a completely different approach: bone retraction! This decision changed my dog's life! Thanks to the doctors' exceptional medical skills, the bone retraction and fixation surgery was successfully performed without bone removal. The post-operative results were excellent. Just one month later, my dog ​​was walking normally and was back to being playful! Its leg had healed completely, and it's living happily again. We are deeply grateful to the doctors and nurses at Chotana Animal Hospital: Truly outstanding treatment skills: While other hospitals gave up and recommended amputation, the medical team here successfully performed a complex bone retraction surgery. Truly attentive to the pet's happiness: When planning treatment, the doctors fully consider the dog's quality of life and future happiness, choosing the method that best facilitates recovery, not just a "fixative solution." Friendly and compassionate team: The doctors and nurses are kind, gentle, and very friendly to pets, making both us and our dog feel safe. Reasonable and transparent pricing: Despite the high level of complexity of the surgery and treatment, the cost was very reasonable and fair. My dog's full recovery is thanks to Chotana Animal Hospital and its expert and responsible doctors! He was so lucky, and our family is incredibly grateful. If you are in Chiang Mai and need reliable pet care, especially for complex bone issues, I highly recommend Chotana Animal Hospital!

0x3050370c7192c063_0x77d86619923c4a7a.text: My experience at Miracles of Asia Rehabilitation Center has truly changed my life. From the very beginning, the owner personally picked me up from the airport, which immediately set the tone for the level of care and dedication this program provides. I stayed for over 60 days, and I have never experienced such genuine concern for my safety, mental health, and sobriety anywhere else. The staff, counselors, therapists, and the clinical director are without question the best mental health professionals I have ever encountered. They use a multi-faceted recovery approach that addresses the mind, body, and spirit. Justin brings incredibly valuable Buddhist techniques he studied for several years in India, which have become essential tools in my recovery. Joe, the clinical director, is a U.S. veteran who worked for the Veterans Affairs system, and his experience, leadership, and understanding of trauma—especially for veterans—is unmatched. What truly sets this place apart is that the counselors and staff come from all walks of life, and many are in recovery themselves. They don’t just teach recovery—they live it. They genuinely understand my struggles. Kane a licensed psychotherapist, opened my mind to new perspectives and practical tools I can use every day to stay sober. Danny, who has worked the 12 Steps and has been sober longer than I’ve been alive, brings a light-hearted but deeply knowledgeable approach. He taught me how to work the 12 Steps properly, how to attend meetings, conduct myself, and most importantly, how to prevent relapse from alcohol and marijuana. Although this is a 5-star luxury rehab, it is still affordable for veterans. I did not have to pay a single dollar—my treatment was billed through the U.S. Department of Veterans Affairs. I strongly encourage any soldiers, sailors, or veterans who are struggling to seek out this program. They can help you with anything you are dealing with. The accommodations are beyond incredible: private luxury rooms, private pools, and the best food I’ve had in Thailand—honestly some of the best food I’ve had anywhere. The classes helped me take a deep, introspective look at my life and begin healing the trauma that led me to drink and smoke in the first place. There are nurses and therapists on staff 24/7, providing constant support. They respect personal beliefs and allow you to attend the church of your choice on Sundays. Every weekend includes amazing outings—whitewater rafting, James Bond Island, elephant sanctuaries, beach barbecues, temples, and caves. Every Saturday, we go to the beach and enjoy Michelin-star-rated meals at places like the Gibbon Sanctuary. They also take you to the best gym and spa in Phuket, where Thai Olympic athletes train. The small process groups were especially important for me because I have social anxiety. Being in groups of three or four people allowed me to open up and safely discuss deep trauma. Through this, I made lifelong connections and realized I am not alone in what I’ve been through. I am actively in recovery today, and I know with certainty that I will never drink alcohol or smoke marijuana again. I owe a debt to this program that I can never fully repay. Miracles of Asia gave me my life back. If you are struggling—especially if you are a veteran—this place can save your life.
0x3050370c7192c063_0x77d86619923c4a7a.author: Zachary Abbott

0x3050370c7192c063_0x77d86619923c4a7a.text: I've just spent an incredible two months of healing, revitalisation and self discovery at Miracles Asia. Words don't quite suffice in attempting to describe what my experience was at this incredible place. But, I'll give it a go. Firstly, Miracles is more of a family and a village rather than a 'treatment facility'. It certainly fits the prerequisite of being a top class treatment facility, though. The experienced staff that have been carefully cultivated are in my opinion of the highest calibre. High levels of mental health and addiction oriented specialisation/education, professionalism, discretion, a depth of experience in the field of addiction, high standards of practical knowledge and most of all genuine compassion, kindness, humour, humility and good intentions. When I say it's like a family it's because from the minute you arrive you are taken into the fold and embraced as one of the 'tribe'. When you arrive from your country of origin you are met at the airport with VIP service and in my case with a warm embrace from the Managing Director, Mark. From here you are taken by the driver to your home for your early recovery journey to begin. Here you are met by friendly warm staff who cater to your every need. Very comfortable, spacious and clean bedrooms that are taken care of daily including having your bed made down at night and warm herbal tea prepared and left in your room to help with having a healthy sleep routine established. It's the little things! From my experience, and from what people that have since left Miracles have said, the kind of individual and groups of people that are attracted to Miracles are special. It is in the groups that the family feel is established through days and weeks of bonding throughout the rigorous program provided there. It is here that you learn an enormous amount about yourself, underlying mental health issues that need addressing and the disease of addiction that you will find most of you have in common. The food is incredible catering to all diets, the grounds are safe and secure leaving you feeling able to be vulnerable allowing the healing to take place, there is a small gymnasium at Miracles to use at your convenience as well as having access to a world class facility nearby complete with an olympic sized swimming pool, chiropractor, physiotherapist and massage therapist and Miracles itself is located in a quiet peaceful part of Phuket surrounded by mountains and jungle making for a tranquil morning walk and peaceful nights sleep, yoga sessions several times a week and the added bonus of getting off grounds on a range of different excursions on Sunday's allowing for exploration of some of the beautiful countryside, restaurants and islands that are all close by. I feel whole, sane and centred after my stay at Miracles and I would definitely recommend it for anyone struggling on their own with addiction issues and ready to seek out help to get your life back on track again.
0x3050370c7192c063_0x77d86619923c4a7a.author: Erik

0x3050370c7192c063_0x77d86619923c4a7a.text: I'm for a few minutes now struggling to write the correct words that will properly encapsulate and vivify my experience at Miracles to the reader. To be frank, it's impossible for me to accurately summarize the last month in such a short text. Alas, let me try :) Miracles Asia is an intimate, luxurious and delicious (the food, of course) facility. The facility is owned and operated by folks in recovery - which I find so compelling and important. Far too often, professionals in the space don't have the go-to solutions that you need to recover because they haven't gone through addiction themselves. Not at Miracles. They have literally "been there, done that." So if there is one thing you can be certain about is that nothing that you say (about your addiction) will shock them. They probably have been through it as well. What also sets Miracles apart is its sheer size. When I was there we were only 4-5 clients, which was AMAZING. I've heard horror stories of other rehabs with 20x that and it's just filled with personality and drama. I got lucky whereby I became great friends with my batch, and even if we didn't mix/get along (which aforementioned, we did - all the time) then at least there was the comfort of privacy and the fact that there was a small group to 'deal' with. I find that addicts in recovery are super sensitive (speaking from experience here) and thus, the less drama the better. Miracle's structure enabled an intimate social environment with superb ratios between staff and clients to boot. That was paramount in my experience, personally. Lastly, this is a private clinic and the prices are - ON THE SURFACE - not cheap. But compared to the rehabs of American or European variety, there is not a better value on the planet. If Miracles was located in the states it would be 3x the price at least. Not to mention, if the price is holding you back - and it's the only thing holding you back - I invite you to reframe your resistance with the following: 1. How much money has your addiction cost you? What is the loss in your opportunity cost? How much are you willing to pay to stop the bleeding? 2. If you had another more 'socially-acceptable' but equally deadly disease like for example Cancer, wouldn't you want to pay top-dollar for a treatment? Think of this as any other treatment for a terminal issue. 3. You really do receive the value that you pay for on a material level. The facility is gorgeous and the staff are so committed, hospitable and kind. I was impressed All in all, it's really a great deal (or dare I say, steal) So in review, my 'top 3' for what sets Miracles apart: 1. First-hand experience of the staff 2. The size 3. Value-for-money. Thank you so much Miracles for setting my sails in the right direction. I will never forget how you changed my life. Cheers
0x3050370c7192c063_0x77d86619923c4a7a.author: R A

0x3050370c7192c063_0x77d86619923c4a7a.text: Unfortunately / fortunately I spent 30 days at another rehab in Bangkok before I went over to miracles . I’ve never been to rehab before and this trip was my only hope at recovery . I had no expectations at the first rehab so I followed the guidelines and did all of the work as suggested but I left there worst off mentally than the day that I got there . My family was tired and they were actually planning to just take me back home when Mark returned a call to my brother and I was on a call with Ryan within a day followed by a video call with Kane and and a personal call with Mark . I had absolutely no expectations going in and honestly I went with a wall up at first because I hated the thought of doing all of the same work again . From the time I walked into miracles I felt protected but also ‘called out’ , which in my opinion is exactly what all addicts need . Addiction is a family disease and at miracles it is treated that way which was a miracle for my family . It’s is by far the most amazing environment to heal in . All of the staff members are amazing and attentive while also being honest and very straightforward which again is EXACTLY what an addict needs . ALL of the luxuries are there for a reason so don’t be fooled lol . …Miracles is for people who WANT to get better ! Not for people who think they are being forced . It cannot work if you do not work , but once you want to be healed then there is NO WAY that you can fail at Miracles . I was lucky enough to have crossed paths with the most amazing bunch of people during my stay . We bonded like family and now have friendships that will last a lifetime . The packed schedule makes it impossible for you to disconnect and trust me …I’ve seen people try very hard to disconnect but the team at miracles has a plan for all of our plans . They’ve thought of everything and their approach is filled with the utmost amount of love and genuine care. If you want to get better , this is the perfect place to do it . It’s not easy …it’s the furthest thing from easy ….but it’s WORTH it ! I couldn’t see a light at all ….my plan was to be dead before the end of the year … God brought me back to life through Miracles . To be honest , getting rid of the drug was the easy part …getting rid of ME was the hard part but It was by far the single most amazing journey that I’ve ever been on . I left miracles as a new member of an exclusive club for humans with super powers (or atleast that’s what I tell my brain lol) …I have a new family …a large one …I have friends all over the world who check on me daily . Thank you to every single person at miracles ! Mark , Boo , Peter ,Maria , Ali , Emmet , Max , Justin , Ash, Kane , and most importantly Di !! I love you guys ….you all are my forever miracles! 🥰🥰 thank you !
0x3050370c7192c063_0x77d86619923c4a7a.author: Anya Elias

0x3050370c7192c063_0x77d86619923c4a7a.text: Miracles was my 3rd private rehab center (yeah, repeat offender on the relapsing). 100+ days out of Miracles and I’m confident that it will be my last rehab center. The staff were warm and professional, competent, qualified, and caring. Some things that set Miracles apart from the other private rehabs I attended: 1) Respect: as a client I was treated like a competent adult that was trying to address a problem, not like an addict that was incapable of making life decisions and needed to be told what to do every moment of the day. 2) In-patient programming: the programming is diverse, relevant and engaging. At each of the other rehabs I felt there was ultimately a lack of programming at the level that could be useful to an adult professional with an addiction issue. In other rehabs the focus is on a different type of clientele that may need education and guidance on the very basics of living a healthy life. 3) Authenticity: while the staff at any rehab I have attended have a caring and patient manner, at Miracles I felt the owners and staff actually, truly cared about me. 4) Community. I greatly appreciated the feeling of belonging to the “Miracles family” while there. On outings, the interactions with the staff that accompany us is more one of peers than of supervisor and supervisees. We all share meals at a common dinner table. I should point out that the food was absolutely amazing. Though the meals are eaten together, for most meals you choose your own dishes from a menu that includes both Thai and international food, prepared by a world-class chef. 5) Exit planning and aftercare: this might be the most critical big difference. At Miracles you leave with a solid exit strategy in place. You get a continuing-care supervisor and a comprehensive after-care package where you zoom into sessions. I still join the evening 12-step meetings by zoom once a week. Miracles is a smaller center, so doesn’t have the extensive facilities of the other 2 centers I attended. There is emphasis on 12-step recovery methods, but also includes cognitive behavioral modalities, mindful meditation and some holistic. Physical fitness is provided by 3 weekly scheduled group trips to a nearby large and comprehensive fitness center (all basic facility use included in your Miracles package)
0x3050370c7192c063_0x77d86619923c4a7a.author: Santa Clause

0x3050370c7192c063_0x77d86619923c4a7a.text: Miracles Asia: A Turning Point in My Recovery Having been through two rehab programs before and relapsing, I didn’t expect much when I found myself on the path to Miracles Asia, my third attempt at rehabilitation. I arrived with little hope that this experience would be any more successful than the last, but I was at rock bottom, desperate for help and ready to find my way out. The staff at Miracles Asia – from the doctor to the therapists, carers, and nurses – are experienced, encouraging, understanding, and genuinely caring. Every member of the team, in every aspect of the program, became someone I deeply appreciated during my stay. They created an environment that promotes a real sense of safety and security. The program itself takes a holistic approach, addressing the mind, body, and spirit. I’m not naturally someone who opens up easily, but the fellowship and bonds formed with the other clients were crucial to my healing. I found myself trusting in the process and in the community, which made all the difference. To be honest, the accommodation and food were the least of my concerns when I arrived – I just wanted a chance at recovery and real solutions. That said, the rooms were lovely and the meals were plentiful, more than adequate for what I needed. When I was ready to make a change, I had to surrender to the process. I’ve now completed the program and am actively using many of the skills I learnt during my time there. While I’ll never be complacent – addiction is a cunning disease – I’ve never felt this free in my life. I feel optimistic and incredibly grateful for each day of sobriety. I no longer miss the sickness, fear, anxiety, and depression that consumed me when I was drinking. I want to deeply thank everyone at Miracles Asia, and the incredible people I had the privilege of sharing my recovery journey with. It was truly a life-changing experience.
0x3050370c7192c063_0x77d86619923c4a7a.author: Lisa Y

0x3050370c7192c063_0x77d86619923c4a7a.text: Miracles has a one of a kind program for all forms of rehabilitation, they came highly recommended from some well established members in society and I too recommend them. They've discovered much about me that I, myself was not aware of. They've managed to breakdown my Strengths, Weaknesses, Opperunities and Threats to a degree that was comprehending and enlightening. I worked on PTSD with therapy, and uncovered allot, it was extremely benificial to my recovery and rediscovery of who I am. Moreover, the activities that we participated in as a group really allowed the mind and soul to reunite with with each other, through each other, for each other. At first, I was Resentful and anxious to get to be alone and through with the excursions, yoga sessions, group meetings and sessions... But a few weeks in, no more than 3, I found my self to be in the total opposite and in need of such activities to de-stress myself and re-enter or ground myself. I completed the 60 day program, which was initially a 30 day program, but 28 days in it was recommended I extend another 30.This was not hard to absorb, I knew that I was in a place and with people who truly cared for my wellbeing and their support was far beyond what I had expected from such a establishment. It's not about business here as much as it's about the true heart felt love and care you receive. Advise I can give anyone who is considering rehabilitation, wellness or an escape to ground one's self and reunite with purpose and recharge for the days to come, is to ; 1. Check out Miracles (personally if you can), with an open heart and mind 2. Listen to the members here, the seniors and the experienced... They'll get you where you need to be and more! Best of luck to you all and my love goes out to Mark&Boo, Bill, Kirstine, Anuke, Denise, Pom (chef) & his support kitchen staff.
0x3050370c7192c063_0x77d86619923c4a7a.author: Eb Farah

0x3050370c7192c063_0x77d86619923c4a7a.text: Miracles is truly an amazing rehab! It’s not only got me sober, but learnt me how to live a happy sober life! I truly never thought it could of been possible. But it’s all 100% true, and I’m still around to tell the tale. I’ve been drinking and taking drugs for over 40 years of my life. After two failed attempts at different rehabs, (one being in Cheshire UK, and the other in Chiang Mai) I checked in to Miracles Phuket. When I cheeked in I was drinking over a litre of whiskey a day. Most of my days was in black-out, and I felt like giving up on life. My first few days is still a blare. But didn’t take long before I started to feel a little better after a few days of controlled detoxing by the lovely nurses every day was getting better and easier. More about Miracles, most of the staff are X alcoholics/addicts which makes a big difference to recovery. It’s quite a small luxury rehab, I think around 18 people. every 4/5 rooms as a private pool so you can relax after a busy day in classes, like meditation, yoga, counselling, morning check-in and evening meeting where someone will tell their story or someone will joint the meeting on zoom and tell their story. (listening to all the stories, really help me on my recovery) not to mention the delicious food cooked chef Mr Pom and his team. (Michelin star) what is really different and special about Miricals. There really do care! And the after care is equally as good, as they continue to keep in touch with you after you leave. I hope anyone who needs help with alcohol or any other kind of drugs, you really should talk with the team at Miracle. And a big thank you to Mark, Danny, Kirsten, Mr Pom (chef) and all the team! You all have really saved my life! I am so grateful and happy!
0x3050370c7192c063_0x77d86619923c4a7a.author: Chris the true critic

0x3102bfb8bd35fb19_0xc216da1ecfe3bdff.text: I'm very afraid of the dentist, and here everything is done to make you feel comfortable. Dr. Arpapan is incredibly kind and gentle; she knew exactly how to put me at ease so I wasn't afraid of having the implant placed. The procedure went perfectly without any pain, and I also want to thank the two assistants who comforted me throughout. I had no post-operative pain and was able to eat an hour after the procedure. I came back a week later, and the implant placement was a complete success. I recommend this clinic to anyone with dental problems, and the prices are very reasonable considering the quality of care and the beauty and cleanliness of the clinic. Thank you again for your kindness and professionalism 🙏
