0x30e290446038e513_0x5dd7cba239f415ad.text: I wanted to send my support to the nurses in the delivery room on the 5th floor of the outpatient building. And thank the doctor who delivered my baby. My baby was in a breech presentation (the doctor was so kind; I had a follow-up appointment for my C-section wound, and the doctor greeted me, remembered me, asked about the baby, inquired about the baby's condition, and even gave me advice on wound care). I was so impressed and grateful. I had booked a private room, but the baby was born with rapid breathing and needed oxygen. The baby needed close contact with doctors and nurses, so I chose to stay with him in the shared delivery room. However, I got to see how attentive all the nurses were to me and my baby. While waiting for the baby's blood test results, I requested to be moved to a private room because the baby could initially be taken off the oxygen machine. Also, the baby's father and relatives wanted to visit and see the baby. So, I gained experience with both shared and private rooms at Bang Yai Hospital. The private rooms are just rooms, nothing special. Checking on the baby was very superficial; for example, weighing the baby – in the shared delivery room, they weighed him without clothes (how attentive they were!), but in the private room, they only weighed him without the swaddling cloth. The weight difference was significant. The doctor assessed the baby and said he could go home without any concerns, just waiting for the blood test results in the afternoon. When I asked at the counter about the private room, the nurse said I could stay another night to wait for the results. But I felt it was wasteful because it was just like sleeping without any check-ups or care, and I wanted to go home because the doctor assessed me in the morning and said there was nothing wrong, so I could leave that day. However, when I told the nurse at the counter, she sounded displeased and had a displeased expression. I would like to see improvements in the private rooms. Everything else was great from my prenatal care to childbirth. Thank you from the bottom of my heart. 🙏🏻
0x30e290446038e513_0x5dd7cba239f415ad.author: bongbawl

0x30e290446038e513_0x5dd7cba239f415ad.text: This was my first time at this hospital for a medical check-up for a job application. I was very impressed with several things: 1. There's a lot of parking space because there's an empty area next to the hospital where you can park. There are also quite a few food stalls (but no shade). 2. The medical check-up wasn't as crowded as I expected. I arrived at the hospital around 7:30 AM. After opening my medical record (which was very easy; just inserting my ID card to verify my identity and handing it to the staff), I waited in front of the specialist clinic on the 4th floor. I put the pink slip I received in the basket and waited. The nurse arrived around 8:30 AM. I was then called in to have my blood pressure taken, my medical history taken, and then sent for various lab tests specified by the company. Mine included a blood test, a urine test, and an X-ray. At the lab, upon arrival, I scanned the barcode on the pink slip and received a queue number (but I recommend informing the staff again beforehand that you also need a urine test). The queue for blood tests didn't take long at all. It might be because it wasn't a medical check-up. I only waited a short time before getting my turn for blood and urine tests. After that, I went to the 3rd floor for an x-ray. Then I came back to the 4th floor to wait for the results. The whole process flowed quite smoothly. There was no waiting around except for the lab results. Once the lab results were out, they called me in to see the doctor to hear the results, receive the medical certificate, and pay. All of this only cost 550 baht. I finished paying at 10:40 AM, so it only took about 3 hours in total. That's very fast for me considering it's a government hospital, because I was mentally prepared to wait 5 hours, haha. 3. All the staff were very nice. No one was rude or aggressive, even though I didn't know anything about what to do or where to go. I was especially impressed with the nurse in the special clinic.
0x30e290446038e513_0x5dd7cba239f415ad.author: pat poppy

0x30e290446038e513_0x5dd7cba239f415ad.text: All the nurses working in the incision ward are very caring and attentive. I received wound care for almost a month (using the 30-baht health insurance, a continuation from a hospital in a provincial area). They observed my wound daily when I had it cleaned, notifying me of any improvement or worsening. If anything seemed abnormal, they would advise me to see a doctor again. After my second visit, the medication and treatment method were changed as the nurses had pointed out. However, I would like to see a fast track option for immediate wound examination by a doctor if any abnormalities are detected. Based on the observations made by the nurses in the incision ward, this would prevent the need to queue again to see a doctor and have the wound cleaned the next day, as the waiting time is very long. This would allow for immediate adjustments to the treatment method. I understand there is a shortage of personnel. Nonthaburi has the highest population, but I would like the hospital management to address this issue. I would also like to see if the number of hospital beds and personnel are sufficient for the population so that additional personnel can be added to alleviate the current staffing levels and reduce waiting times for patients to see doctors. I believe this will allow the hospital to develop faster and more modern treatment methods.
0x30e290446038e513_0x5dd7cba239f415ad.author: Pepe B.

0x30e290446038e513_0x5dd7cba239f415ad.text: 📢 Booking a dental appointment online is very convenient, hassle-free, and fast. It saves a lot of money. The doctor and assistants are lovely. At the scheduled time, you go up to the 4th floor, weigh yourself, have your blood pressure checked, and confirm your appointment. I usually arrive about 15 minutes early, or about an hour early, to have my blood pressure checked again because I have high blood pressure and need it measured multiple times. Almost everything was perfect. ❌ Except for some male doctors who, seeing that a case was difficult, refused to treat it. They went on to treat teeth that weren't specified, even though my medical history clearly indicated which teeth needed treatment (1, 2, 3, 4). 0x305031f0a9d87749_0xc2615a17bd181b04.text: The doctor is excellent! The treatment was great. I had a serum allergy for months, and even hospital visits didn't help. I thought my skin would never recover, but the doctor treated it so well that it's almost completely healed within a week. My skin returned to near-normal within a week. She explained the cause and details very thoroughly, meticulously examining my case and not just superficially. She gave complete instructions on how to care for my skin, outlining what I should and shouldn't do, and which products were suitable or not for specific areas. The staff at the counter seemed a bit stern and assertive, but they were actually very kind. They were always smiling and spoke in a pleasant tone. They always inform you beforehand that they only accept cash, and there's a sign indicating this. You can choose whether or not to receive medication, or just take medication within your budget. I really appreciated their clarity on this point. The page admin responded quickly and efficiently. Parking might be a bit difficult as it's in the old town area. I recommend bringing a motorcycle; it's much easier to find parking. If you come during clinic opening hours, there will be fewer people and the wait won't be long. Highly recommend 👍🏻🫶🏻

0x305031f0a9d87749_0xc2615a17bd181b04.text: I'm a regular customer. I recently went for a check-up because of a skin allergy and inflammation. The doctor and Ms. Da at the counter took good care of me as usual. I requested a medical certificate and receipt for insurance claims without any problems, but I'll pick them up later because there are so many patients and they can't write them all during business hours. It's understandable, I know they're really busy. Regarding payment, they only accept cash; they haven't accepted cards or scanned payments for a long time. Anyone saying they don't accept cash hasn't actually visited the clinic because there's a clear sign at the counter stating "Cash only." Also, Ms. Da at the counter informs you before every appointment. She's usually very friendly to all patients. I can guarantee she would never ask a patient to go to another clinic because she owns the clinic; why would she do that? Anyone accusing her of being rude or asking patients to leave should be careful. Posting false information and slandering others, especially using a fake avatar, could lead to a defamation lawsuit under the Computer Crime Act. The laws are very strict these days.

0x30e29fd1f0b7d2ad_0x3d6adc63668717f0.text: Initially, after reading the reviews for this clinic (there was only one review), I wasn't keen on going here. So I went to the clinic across the street, but the doctor and staff there weren't very good. I had an 11 am appointment, arrived 30 minutes early, and only saw the doctor at 11:30 am. I was even skipped in line! They did an X-ray of my root canal and then explained a lot about the costs. I asked for the X-ray film to take back to Max Dental the next day. It turned out that Dr. Phadet, a specialist in root canal treatment, facial structure, jaw, and nerve disorders related to the tooth roots (Maxilofacial Surgery), is an excellent doctor. My condition: Last year, my lower molar cracked and needed a filling. However, the filling was too large, allowing infection to damage the root. Now, the root behind it is damaged and dry. Currently, two of my front roots are inflamed and infected with pus, caused by the poorly done filling – instead of treating the root canal first, they filled it, leading to the infection. Max Dental's treatment: X-ray analysis of the root canal. Looking at the X-ray, the front tooth root appeared black. The doctor said there was a 50:50 chance of extraction, but after examining the actual tooth, the chances became 70:30 – a possibility of successful treatment without extraction (I was so happy because this is my first time having root canal treatment and I didn't want to lose my molar). Comment: After reviewing the X-ray, the doctor explained how it happened. After examining the actual tooth and analyzing the damage, he explained the treatment options very clearly. He even mentioned that if there was a worst-case scenario involving extraction, I shouldn't worry because they had done their best. Furthermore, the cost of the root canal treatment today can be claimed for a prosthetic or crown later, which I think is very fair. I'm glad I met a truly skilled doctor, not just a commercialist. As Confucius said, "Doctors who talk a lot are for business; those who don't talk much are for genuine and thorough treatment." This clinic has been open for 10 years, which speaks to their skill, and we shouldn't trust Google Maps reviews too much. If you have problems with tooth roots or molars, I can confirm this clinic is excellent.

0x30e29e987b7ff7f3_0x73ed82f3b274e545.text: Walk-ins are welcome before 10:00 AM for free sterilization; no appointment is needed. There are cancellations every day. While appointments are limited to 50 animals per day, on the day we went, only about 20 animals were actually sterilized. Cancellation surgeries start at 10:00 AM, and patients can go home by 11:00 AM. Open Monday to Friday, closed on public holidays. Remember to withhold food and water from your cat or dog for 12 hours before surgery. Register before 10:00 AM and remember to keep track of the queue to ensure it's within the 50 slots available. This prevents staff from miscounting and claiming it's full, so you can dispute the scheduling. Please bring your ID card (one ID card per two cats or dogs).

A customer asked about the process for filling out forms at home, but the male staff member gave no answer, forcing them to ask others. I highly recommend this place for anyone wanting to microchip their cat or dog. 0x30da3aeea09c3f97_0x7a0de8d26ec8419a.text: This small Clinic called PHA MAI Community Clinic is one of 6 run by Thanyarak Institute & Government Hospital and in charge of Outpatient treatments for dependencies on Alcohol and Heroin* (*methadon treatment) aswell as psychological disbalances. As a government institution their rates are low and affordable (Check rates at the end of review) compared to specialised private clinics like Bangkok Hospital were one pay around 100$/visit + the cost of medicine and get hardly more then 3days M.prescribed They also take care of non Thais, meaning any Farang or foreigner is welcome, and this very devoted team in general has a pretty good command of English. As part of the treatment they deliver 7-15 days Methadon to their patients after a doctor visit and a formal registration.(+ docs *) They offer the possibility of short stays in hospital and to stay as an inpatient in a post-cure. A basic understanding in Thai language is required for a post cure. Offering a fast, discreet, understanding & professional service they are actualy among the few(+ **) to offer such an affordable methadon treatment in Chiang Mai. This clinic itself is only for outgoing patient and treats also other addictions like Alcohol and other psychological imbalances Open on Monday to Saturday : 08.00 to 16.30 Dr Vsits from 09h00 to 11h00 only Monday-Tuesday Doctor Visit: 200bth Methadon: 1bath/1cc (This rate for foreigners only/ Thai people don't pay) +* Certificat from former treating Doctor is a plus . +** A similar clinic in CMai is 'PANU MD.Clinic' check on Google Map for full review! There are 6 other Thayanrak Methadon Clinics in Thailand: Bangkok, MaeHongSon, Puket, Chiang Mai and 2 other major cities.

0x30da3aeea09c3f97_0x7a0de8d26ec8419a.text: This is a great place. Much cheaper than the big hospitals. They speak English fairly well and charge farrang 1baht per mg. Free to citizens. I also get 84 mg of alprazolam for about 450 baht. So I pay 1450 thb every 4 weeks for 1000 mg of methadone and 84 mg of alprazolam. This was over 6k baht at Bangkok Hospital. The first time I went I had to go to the main location about 30 minute drive north of old city. I had extensive paperwork from my doctor's in the states. You would definitely need that as alprazolam is strictly controlled. I go every 4 weeks for a refill. During non covid it was every 2 weeks. Always keep your pink card they give you on your person. Methadone is controlled and your pink card is basically proof of your prescription. It takes 5 to 10 minutes every trip. Very fast and friendly.

The silicone is brown in color, suitable for people with little nasal flesh or thin skin because when light hits it, the silicone will not reflect light clearly. Normally, Thais like to augment their noses with silicone nose rods. It will be augmented along the entire length of the bridge to the tip of the nose. For some patients with little nasal flesh and thin skin, the doctor must be careful about the tip of the nose, which is the most prone area to perforation. Therefore, artificial tissue materials are used to support the tip of the nose to prevent the silicone from directly touching the silicone rod and the skin of the tip of the nose. This reduces the risk of a perforated nose or a thin tip, and also makes the nose shape more beautiful and proportionate. Sloping nose surgery is a nose tip that is raised up. This nose shape is the opposite of the teardrop nose. It is a nose shape that requires nose augmentation with a decorated tip. 0x30e29ef562923039_0x47d1fdba6ab4cd1c.text: I am a patient at Dr. Saim's Clinic. I started treatment because of an allergic rash that I had never had before. I had previously gone to a traditional Chinese medicine practitioner who said my kidneys weren't functioning properly. I spent several months and tens of thousands of baht on Chinese medicine, and my condition only slightly improved. Then I learned about Gua Sha and Dr. Saim's Clinic from Pantip (a Thai online forum) and old videos of Dr. Saim appearing on TV. I decided to try Gua Sha with Dr. Saim, initially just wanting to cure the rash. The results have been amazing; my internal systems have become stronger, my overall health has improved, and I still see the doctor occasionally. The treatment is the same for all patients: Gua Sha scraping at the problem areas and taking Thai medicine recommended by the doctor (you can refuse the medicine if you wish). The scraping isn't done haphazardly; the doctor scrapes the problem areas according to traditional Thai medicine principles (the level of pain depends on the individual's problem). The doctor's medicine is limited, mainly: - Laxatives: These are detoxifying agents that remove waste from the body. Their potency varies (varying from person to person). My case was very severe. Initially, I fainted, vomited, and had diarrhea all night, barely sleeping. My stool was black and very foul-smelling. After taking them continuously, the color changed to yellow. And it's odorless. - The doctor recommended taking the liquid and tablet medicines together, as a tonic and a treatment. The taste is terrible and difficult to swallow, but that's understandable because it's the natural taste of the medicine itself, without added flavors or scents. The doctor's medicine is safe because I previously bought a steroid test kit from the Ministry of Public Health and it didn't detect any steroids. Therefore, before you decide to seek treatment at Saiim Traditional Thai Medicine Clinic, you must ask yourself: 1. Are you sick and want to improve your health? 2. Based on what you've read above, do you think you can follow the doctor's treatment plan? If the answer is "yes," call to schedule an appointment with the doctor. It's painful, but it's worth it in the long run.

0xacb7bf244b5f3911_0x6f78e398b5ca6c94.text: I've been bringing my two children here for dental care for almost a year now (spending over 20,000 RMB, because their teeth were completely decayed. I initially wanted to give them more control, but now I regret it; the cost of trial and error is too high. You really have to find a balance). I live in Sansai, which is quite far from here. I came here last year with a doctor, but ended up meeting another doctor, who is also the owner—Dr. Praew. I've also had my teeth cleaned, filled, and wisdom teeth extracted here. Everyone is very friendly, and I don't have any fear of going to the dentist. Last Saturday, I suddenly had a lot of pain in my back teeth. Since appointments are required here, I desperately went to a clinic in Sansai. They diagnosed me with root canal treatment, but there was a waiting list. I felt they weren't very professional, so I left. I called Happy Bear on a whim (because the pain was so bad I wanted immediate help). The receptionist said the appointment was for the next day. Feeling the pain was unbearable, I asked her to ask Dr. Praew what could help alleviate the pain. She said she'd check and get back to me. A little while later, I received a call from Dr. Praew, who told me to come in that afternoon so they could handle it before they closed. I was so touched. When I arrived, the doctor said the X-ray taken at the clinic that morning was too blurry and needed to be redone. Everyone was working overtime for me; it was truly heartwarming. After the X-ray, the doctor examined it and said my pulp was fine and I didn't need root canal treatment, but the periodontal pockets needed cleaning because it had been six months since the last cleaning, and the current pain might be caused by that. What would have cost over 10,000 baht was resolved for only 460 baht. It's Thursday today, and after a few days, my toothache has subsided, with only a slight swelling. Here, I felt the care of friends and the respect shown to patients. I said I didn't want anesthesia, and the doctor supported me. I said I didn't want painkillers, and the doctor prescribed a few just in case. I would recommend this dental clinic to friends living in Hangdong, but not to those living in Sansai—it's really too far. However, I come regularly, so the distance is acceptable.
0xacb7bf244b5f3911_0x6f78e398b5ca6c94.author: lin yang

Therefore, I would like to change my rating from one star last year to five stars, because I don't want to discourage other dedicated staff members from a negative review (and I don't want one bad apple to spoil the whole barrel). * 23/1/69 at 13:30, the head nurse called to inquire about further details. I explained what I had experienced, but despite my attempts to explain the service I received, she seemed to understand, yet not quite. She seemed sympathetic, but not quite. Furthermore, she implied that I must be rich to not care about the department specified on the referral slip, which is irrelevant. If the doctor doesn't specify the disease to be treated, I cannot use my insurance. I understand that, but my post was only about the "service," and I want that to be understood as well. Ultimately, calling to inquire didn't improve the situation; it just made me more frustrated... * The person taking the history was extremely rude. It was only the first person in line; what was the rush? Didn't they read the documents, or were they illiterate? When I pointed this out, they ignored me and said, "The doctor will check it later." Why ask in the first place? Their facial expression and tone were as if I had to beg them. Someone in this role should at least be humane, not a robot asking questions. 0x3054f1052fe64571_0x9cd3cdfb4ff4ed16.text: Review for Dental Solution at Bangkok Hospital, Koh Samui I can only praise the all-round service at Dental Solution in Bangkok Hospital, Koh Samui. First of all, I was able to get an appointment at very short notice. My issue was an inflamed tooth root, with swollen and extremely painful gums. I was given an appointment on the same day, and everything was explained to me transparently. X-rays were taken, and the further treatment options were discussed in detail. I was presented with three choices, and after making a decision, the procedure was carried out promptly. Just one and a half hours later, I was pain-free and on my way back to the hotel. By the evening, I was already able to resume all my activities, and I have been pain-free ever since. A huge compliment to the entire team, especially Dr. Wanwimon Potjanatkomon, who treated me with great care and professionalism, and Joy, the assistant, who was incredibly competent and efficient. Joy had already communicated with me in the morning via WhatsApp, providing excellent support and ensuring a smooth process. Her English skills were outstanding, making everything even easier. The whole team was absolutely excellent – highly recommended for anyone in need of professional and efficient dental care!

0x30e29fc0b64f55d5_0x92e8a346f1e0633f.text: (Please read to the end for guidance for those considering this service. I've explained every step so it will be helpful for everyone.) ❤️ From someone who just had the vacuum extraction service yesterday, I can say it wasn't as scary or painful as I thought. It was like menstrual cramps, just a tight, heavy feeling. The procedure (the suction part) probably took less than 5 minutes. Before the procedure, the doctor's words helped to alleviate my stress and anxiety, which was great. The doctor explained everything to me throughout the process. Thank you! (P.S. The assistant who administered the anesthesia also chatted with me, asking where I was from, which was very relaxing.) I thought it would be more painful, but it was much less than I expected. 🙏🏻 As for the procedure itself, it's quite long because there are many steps involved (I recommend eating beforehand). I went on a Saturday, and my case took 4 hours to complete because there were 3 patients ahead of me. My appointment was at 2:40 PM, but I arrived at 2:00 PM. (It's okay to arrive early so you can get a queue number, have your blood pressure checked, and be allowed to drink water beforehand to relieve yourself and hold your urine once for the ultrasound.) After the ultrasound, the assistant will draw blood to check blood concentration. Then, drink 2 liters of water until your urine is clear. Once it's clear, urinate and take a picture to show the counter staff (this step takes quite a long time; you'll drink 2 liters until your stomach is bloated). After taking the picture of your clear urine, wait to be called for a sarong to change into. Drink one bottle of electrolyte solution (available for purchase at the clinic). After drinking the electrolyte solution, you'll receive a set of medication, about 5 pills. The medication is quite strong, so it's recommended to eat beforehand (this whole process takes 3 hours). Around 5:00 PM, the counter staff started calling people to go up to the 3rd floor. However, there weren't just people getting the procedure done; there were also those picking up medication and likely those getting ultrasounds. We went up to the 3rd floor around 5:40 PM (it's recommended to bring a bag to put your underwear, sanitary pads, and tissues in). We were called into the room around 6:00 PM. The doctor will have you urinate again before getting on the table. After that, they'll administer anesthesia and perform the procedure. After it's finished, you'll change back into the underwear you came in. That's it. (The assistant will take pictures of the ultrasound before and after the procedure with your phone.) I sat and waited while the assistant explained the various effects and post-procedure self-care guidelines. I scanned the remaining payment upstairs and then went down to go home… P.S. All the staff, including the doctor, were very kind and polite. No one was rude or aggressive. I was very impressed. Just following the procedures makes it easy. I was very scared during the 4 hours I spent in the clinic before the procedure; my heart was racing. But after it was over, everything felt so relieved. Thank you so much. (If you're driving, I recommend parking at Center One mall and walking across the pedestrian bridge. It's not far.) That's all I wanted to share about my experience. I hope it's helpful for everyone. ⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️
0x30e29fc0b64f55d5_0x92e8a346f1e0633f.author: Jai Dee

0x30e29fc0b64f55d5_0x92e8a346f1e0633f.text: I give it 5 stars! The nurses all worked incredibly hard. Cases finished at 1 or 2 AM – they were amazing! The doctor explained everything well and followed the procedures. If the patient wasn't feeling well, they wouldn't force them, demonstrating professionalism and a gentle touch. 📍Recommendations from my actual experience📍 - I recommend arriving on time for your appointment to avoid long waits. - Park at Center One mall and remember to get your parking ticket stamped; it's 30% cheaper than not stamping it. - I recommend bringing someone with you in case they need to buy water or food. But if you must go alone, I recommend preparing everything you need: water, snacks, sanitary pads, charging cable, power bank. - Wearing a dress is easiest; you don't need to change, just put on a sarong for the quickest process. - I recommend eating a little before taking the medication (after the ultrasound) otherwise you might vomit because the antibiotics can irritate the stomach. - Smelling salts, balm, and a warm jacket are must-haves. - The wait is quite long, depending on the previous cases. If a case can't be performed, the nurses will ask you to wait. So, it might not be as quick as you'd like, so be patient and don't complain. - Drink plenty of water throughout the procedure. Dehydration can prevent the procedure from being performed. - If you have a panic attack and experience symptoms before the procedure, the doctor will monitor your symptoms and may recommend whether or not to proceed. - It depends on the patient's decision, but medication may be recommended instead (medication is 95% effective, vacuum suction is 100% effective). - Total cost is 4,500 baht (300 baht deposit, 4,200 baht payable after the procedure). - The procedure isn't scary. There will be a strange tingling sensation in the lower abdomen, some slight discomfort, and a dull ache, but it's not excruciatingly painful. Those who have had surgery before will be able to mentally prepare themselves. - There's no blood splatter, it's not scary. The room is bright, clean, and odorless. The atmosphere is like a typical clinic, not gruesome. - The nurses are very helpful from start to finish, providing excellent advice and care. 📍Finally, for everyone who goes through with this procedure, please don't blame yourselves. Just going through the procedure already makes you feel unwell, there's no need to blame yourself and add to your negative feelings. Live your life to the fullest and be cautious. Take vitamins and supplements, keep your body healthy, do good deeds to find peace of mind but don't let it become a sin. Do everything you want to do, and encourage yourself a lot. ✌🏻 Hopefully, this review will help many people.
0x30e29fc0b64f55d5_0x92e8a346f1e0633f.author: Kayu

0x30e29fc0b64f55d5_0x92e8a346f1e0633f.text: This might be helpful for those deciding whether to get medication 💊 - I got two faint lines on the pregnancy test (tested twice). - I added the clinic's LINE account, consulted, and booked an appointment to pick up medication in the morning, finishing almost at noon 🕝 - The clinic is very cold, so bring a jacket 🥶 - Upon arrival, register, fill out your medical history, and have your blood pressure checked. - Drink enough water to feel the urge to urinate, then hold it in (do not urinate). There's a reason why you need to drink a lot of water and hold your urine during the ultrasound. Try searching for the reason on the internet. - The staff called me up to wait on the 3rd floor. - I went in for the ultrasound with the doctor. - The doctor was kind and explained things well. If you're unsure, you can search the doctor's name online. They are a real gynecologist 👨🏻‍⚕️ - The ultrasound didn't show anything clear, it was very small. The doctor let me decide whether to wait another month for another ultrasound or to get the medication now. ⚠️ You'll sit and talk with the staff here to test your ability, knowledge, and understanding to see if you've read and understood the information. ⚠️ The staff at this point are quite strict, even a bit stern. It's like a Thai language teacher ready to hit you with a stick at any moment if you answer wrong, too slowly, or don't answer the question directly or to the point. You shouldn't beat around the bush; answer directly, concisely, and to the point. Don't stress. Be patient, we'll get through this. ⚠️Pay for medication, add the LINE account for the support team while using medication. ⚠️We recommend watching the doctor's videos, videos about potential side effects, and information about the medication thoroughly until you understand it. -Going home 🏡 I have one child already and raise him/her 24/7. I understand the exhaustion. My child just started school, and I was about to go back to work, but this baby came at a time when I wasn't ready, so I decided to terminate the pregnancy. I have to accept what happened, but I shouldn't blame myself. Is it sin? Does it really exist? It would be a huge sin if the child had to be born and I couldn't raise them. Being able to raise them well means not just raising them day by day. Regarding the post-medication review, I don't know yet because I haven't taken it, but it will probably be painful, but I can handle it. P.S. Everyone shouldn't blame themselves. 0x30e29fc0b64f55d5_0x92e8a346f1e0633f.text: I had an appointment for 7:10 PM and arrived about 20 minutes early. The procedure finished around 11 PM. I recommend eating and drinking beforehand if you want it to be over quickly. Also, bring two large bottles of water because the doctor will ask you to drink 2 liters and urinate until your urine is clear, then take a picture to show the doctor. If you're having vacuum aspiration, prepare electrolyte solution or a sugar drink. Water and tissues are available for purchase if you didn't bring any. Once your urine is clear, inform the doctor. However, my procedure took longer because I was nervous, causing them to check my blood pressure and pulse multiple times because they were too high. The nurse had me drink more water and then check again. I had them check about 5 times before my blood pressure and pulse went down. Then they took an ultrasound to review the images before the procedure. After that, they gave me medication and I waited another 15 minutes. Then I informed the doctor. Once the time was up, I waited to be called for the procedure. The actual procedure takes about 15 minutes. During the procedure, I felt abdominal pain similar to menstrual cramps, but maybe a little tingling. After the procedure and the equipment was removed, I was able to stand up immediately, but I had a little pain in my lower left abdomen. I could walk normally, there was no burning sensation, and there was very little bleeding. After the procedure, they'll explain the post-procedure instructions, and then you can go home. The nurses were very nice and not as scary as I thought. They kept encouraging me. I was impressed that throughout the procedure, no doctor or nurse was rude. Everyone smiled and spoke in a very friendly manner. There are very few seats, so I recommend that if you bring a relative or partner, you should wait outside. When I came, half the room was occupied by men, and I had to walk around to find a chair.
0x30e29fc0b64f55d5_0x92e8a346f1e0633f.author: Morfreen Morphine

0x30e29fc0b64f55d5_0x92e8a346f1e0633f.text: My boyfriend and I experienced an unexpected event. After discussing it, we decided to terminate the pregnancy. We searched online for information and found this doctor's clinic. We sent our information late Friday night. The doctor contacted us Saturday morning to book an appointment via the green app. We booked and luckily got a Saturday appointment. Before coming, I read reviews and found that most were positive. The low-star reviews mostly concerned waiting times and negative experiences with the nurses. In reality, everyone was very caring, although some were a little strict, as is typical of nurses. Overall, everything went very well. Thank you to the doctor and nurses for your care. Our appointment was at 7:50 PM, but we arrived a little early in case of registration. The entire process was completed around 1:30 AM, taking a total of 5.5 hours. The clinic provided water, tissues, and electrolyte solution. The process went something like this: First part: 1. Registration 2. Basic health check 3. Waiting for ultrasound. Finished around 9:30 PM (a little over an hour from registration). Second part: [After ultrasound] [During this time, you can eat. If you're alone, bring snacks or food, or you can walk out to eat nearby. There are 7-Eleven stores, coffee shops, and shopping malls nearby. / Bring headphones or a tablet to download content to watch while you wait. / The air conditioning in some areas is very cold because it can get hot when there are many people. If there are few people, it might be very cold. / If you're coming from far away, there are many accommodations nearby.] 4. Go down and have some water while you wait. 5. Wait in line for medication. 6. Drink electrolyte solution. 7. Undergo the procedure. I offer my encouragement to everyone who has to make this decision, and I thank the doctor for giving me this opportunity.
0x30e29fc0b64f55d5_0x92e8a346f1e0633f.author: C P

0x30e29fc0b64f55d5_0x92e8a346f1e0633f.text: Based on my personal experience, I went on the 26th. The doctor and nurses were lovely and friendly, which made the experience stress-free. -For those driving their own car, honestly, there's no parking. We parked at Center One mall across the street and walked across the pedestrian bridge. Parking costs 40 baht per hour. You can park right away; you don't need to wait for the mall to open. -I recommend arriving on time. You should arrive about 20 minutes early, but no earlier, as they serve patients on a first-come, first-served basis. Arriving exactly at your booked time is best. -Upon arrival, open your booking confirmation on LINE and show your ID card to the counter staff. Then, sit and wait for a short while. The nurse will give you a queue number. -Don't bring too many people, as this might take up too many seats. It's best to bring only one person to look after you. -I recommend drinking plenty of water while waiting to speed things up (drinking lots of water helps ensure your urine is clear). -Things to bring: Two 1-liter bottles of water, sanitary pads, tissues, and a phone charger. The clinic provides free charging outlets if you bring your own charger. If you don't bring one, you won't be served. It costs 20 baht per visit. Sanitary pads and water bottles are available for purchase at the clinic. -I recommend eating 1-2 hours before the procedure because the nurse will give you medication. If you don't eat beforehand, you might vomit. -After the nurse examines you and the doctor performs the ultrasound, you need to wait until your urine is clear before taking the medication given by the nurse. That's all I wanted to recommend. I want everyone to not worry and not stress. The doctor is lovely and kind.
0x30e29fc0b64f55d5_0x92e8a346f1e0633f.author: Pee Pee

0x30e29fc0b64f55d5_0x92e8a346f1e0633f.text: I hope this review helps anyone who's hesitant. I had an appointment at 9:40 AM, but didn't get to do it until 11 AM. The delay was because I had to drink a lot of water to get my urine clear (lol). It wouldn't stay clear for a while! I went through two large bottles of water. Luckily, my urine was clear, so the procedure went faster. If you want to go quickly, drink plenty of water beforehand! The staff were great; they joked around to keep me from feeling stressed. Upon arrival, they checked my blood pressure, took blood samples, and did an ultrasound to determine my baby's gestational age. The clinic had me change into a gauze pad and take medication while I waited in line. I should mention that it seems easier for those with lower gestational ages, judging from what the staff said. I was 9 weeks pregnant. Once in, the doctor was excellent. She clearly explained everything: what she was doing, what would be inserted, what would be injected. A nurse sat with me and gave me smelling salts. And importantly, she chatted with me! The nurse chatted with me during the procedure, asking where I was from and where I lived (lol). It helped ease my mind. There was background music in the room, and the staff were chatting happily (lol). During the procedure, I felt some tightness. I felt a dull ache in my lower abdomen, but there wasn't as much bleeding as I expected. Afterward, the doctor showed me before and after photos. It took less than 5 minutes. I just rested, changed clothes, and went home. I went in alone, but my boyfriend's mother waited outside because the clinic was very crowded. The doctor was very polite, and the nurses were lovely. I hope this review helps you all in your decision-making! ✌🏻
